definition: In this source, assisted living refers to a long-term residential care setting where people live as residents. It is described as a place in which psychological interventions can be delivered.

reasons: The packet supports that assisted living residents are studied in a long-term residential care context, but it does not define assisted living as a care setting where psychological interventions can be delivered.
The definition adds an implementation claim about psychological interventions that is not stated in the source packet.

The packet does not explicitly define what “assisted living” refers to (e.g., it does not state “assisted living refers to …”), and only uses the term in describing study context ("assisted living residents").

The claim that it is a “long-term residential care setting” is only supported in the packet as the phrase “long-term residential care” (feasibility underexplored), but the packet does not directly connect that phrase as the definition of “assisted living.”

The claim that assisted living is “a place in which psychological interventions can be delivered” is only indirectly implied by the study using DBT-ST among assisted living residents; the packet does not explicitly state this as a definitional characterization of assisted living.
